scope: Public-source metadata review extending the Federal Reserve/FBI/White House-related crime research into the 1920s (1920-1929).
coverage_note: This is a source and metadata inventory, not a claim that every 1920s criminal record has been scanned. Federal investigative recordkeeping changed over time, and many records remain archival, restricted, or incompletely described online.

chronology.1920: FBI documents the September 16, 1920 Wall Street bombing near the U.S. Assay Office and J.P. Morgan building. The FBI notes that more than 30 people were killed initially and approximately 300 injured; responsibility was not immediately established.
chronology.1921: The FBI Central Records System was established and later modified as the Bureau assumed additional responsibilities. NARA's RG 65 contains FBI investigative records from this period.
chronology.1924: NARA records show Classification 29 (Bank Fraud and Embezzlement) was established in 1924 for investigations into fraud against financial institutions protected by federal statutes. The Bureau's central filing system also incorporated predecessor records around this period.
chronology.1924_civil_rights: NARA states Classification 44 was established in a January 1924 Hoover memorandum; early files primarily concerned Ku Klux Klan activity and civil-rights violations.
chronology.1929: Federal Reserve historical statistical tables include year-end banking-system data for 1929, useful as financial/economic metadata but not as crime records.

source_collections.source: National Archives RG 65 - FBI Central Records
NARA Classification 29 - Bank Fraud and Embezzlement

interpretation_rules: Do not treat archival classification as evidence that a person committed a crime
A record's existence does not establish guilt
A missing online catalog entry does not mean a record was destroyed
Separate historical financial statistics from criminal investigative records
Do not infer contents of restricted/classified records
Preserve the distinction between federal jurisdiction and state/local investigations
The 1920 Wall Street bombing should be recorded as an investigated historical bombing; attribution must follow documented evidence rather than inference
status: 1920s public-source archival metadata extension prepared for Prev_NW.
